Summary.Title: Regulated Object Identity Schema
Summary.IdentityAuthorityBoundary: The Regulated Object Identity schema defines canonical object identity, source-system bindings, aliases, verification, duplicate resolution, relationships, lifecycle, physical-digital binding, integrity, holds, and identity passports. It has no independent approval, release, override, execution, or official-record authority.
Summary.HumanAuthorityRule: Qualified humans and authorized organizational roles remain accountable for identity verification, duplicate resolution, lifecycle decisions, and binding actions.
Summary.SourceOfTruthRule: Official object records remain in governed source systems.
Summary.Step154Statement: Step 154 defines a Regulated Object Identity schema baseline. It does not implement runtime identity services, modify existing architecture, validate production systems, merge real records, or authorize regulated execution.
Summary.Step155Gate: READY AFTER STEP 154 REGULATED OBJECT IDENTITY SCHEMA REVIEW

Invariants.Rule: Every governed object must resolve to one stable canonical object_id.

Invariants.InvariantName: Canonical Identity Is Not Display Text
Invariants.Rule: Names, labels, filenames, routes, and display values must not serve as the sole canonical identity.
Official-state claims must include a governed source-system identity binding.

Invariants.InvariantName: Aliases Do Not Replace Canonical Identity
Invariants.Rule: Aliases may resolve to a canonical object but must not silently create or replace canonical identity.
Suspected duplicates remain unresolved until a governed human or rule-based resolution is completed and recorded.
Active, held, suspended, superseded, retired, recalled, archived, and other lifecycle states must not be inferred from absence.
Object relationships must reference valid canonical identities and supporting evidence.
QR, NFC, RFID, barcode, BLE, certificate, sensor, and wearable bindings must be governed, attributable, current, and evidence-backed.
Material identity mismatch, duplication, ambiguity, or source conflict must create an explicit governance hold.
Active regulated objects require an identifiable owner, steward, or authorized organizational role.
The identity schema does not replace official records in governed source systems.

Invariants.InvariantName: Display Does Not Create Identity Authority
Invariants.Rule: Thread D, Thread D2, RAMAT Vision, glasses, wearables, dashboards, and witnesses may display identity state but may not create, merge, retire, approve, or override canonical identity.

Components.Purpose: Defines the single governed identity record representing a regulated, critical, operational, physical, digital, human, AI, document, transactional, or evidence-bearing object.
Components.RequiredFields: object_id; object_type_id; canonical_name; lifecycle_state; identity_status; owner_role_id; steward_role_id; created_at_utc; updated_at_utc
Components.ValidationRule: Every governed object must have one stable canonical object_id that does not depend only on a mutable name, label, route, display value, filename, or local alias.
Components.Examples: Clinical subject, specimen, batch, equipment item, CI, AI agent, shipment, serialized product, document, transaction, dose, or case.
Components.IdentityAuthorityBoundary: The schema identifies, binds, verifies, relates, and governs regulated objects. It does not independently approve, release, override, execute, or authorize regulated actions.
Components.SourceOfTruthRule: Official object records remain in governed source systems. The identity schema stores canonical references, bindings, aliases, verification results, integrity values, relationships, and governance states without replacing the official source record.
Components.HumanAccountabilityRule: A designated object owner, data steward, system owner, process owner, Quality Unit, clinical authority, or other authorized human role remains accountable for identity verification and binding decisions.
Components.DisplayBoundary: Thread D, Thread D2, RAMAT Vision, glasses, wearables, dashboards, and device witnesses may display object identity state but may not create, approve, merge, retire, release, or override canonical identity.
Components.DataBoundary: Schema-only, simulator-first, mock-data-first, and local-validation-first. No PHI, company production data, classified data, or real regulated production integration is authorized by this step.
Components.Step155Dependency: Evidence, authority, No-Bind, accountability, and admissibility records must reference a valid canonical object_id.
Components.MaturityStatement: Identity schema registration is not runtime implementation, production readiness, regulatory validation, certification, or operational release.
